page.title: Crystal Hint

single.avgHint: Averaging neighbouring patterns suppresses per-pixel noise and roughly doubles the symmetry NCC on real EBSD data. Use single pixel if the area has grain boundaries within ±2 pixels.
single.edsWeightingTooltip: Use measured EDS chemistry to break ties: off, soft weighting, or hard filter.
single.edsHint: Uses the pixel's measured EDS chemistry to break ties pattern symmetry can't (e.g. Al vs Al2Cu vs α-Al(Fe,Mn)Si). Soft damps the score by chemistry match; Filter drops chemically inconsistent phases. Needs a dataset with co-located EDS (h5oina) — otherwise falls back to pattern-only with a notice.

single.fileReadyHint: Open an EBSD file first (EBSD Viewer or HDF5 Viewer tab).

quality.title: Quality check
quality.intro: For each pixel: compares the detected pattern symmetry (n-fold via rotation NCC) against the indexed phase's expected crystal system. Flags mismatches as likely misindexing or missing-phase candidates.
quality.maxPixelsTooltip: Cap analysed pixels for the quality check; whole scan is sub-sampled to this.
quality.avgRadiusTooltip: Per-pixel averaging radius to make the mismatch count more reliable.
quality.avgRadiusHint: Per-pixel averaging — smooths symmetry detection so the mismatch count is more reliable.
quality.runTooltip: Compare each pixel's detected symmetry with its indexed phase to find misindexing.
quality.noIndexingHint: No active indexing result — run /Indexing first, then return here.
quality.placeholder: Run quality check to compare each pixel's detected symmetry against its indexed phase. Mismatches are likely misindexed or signal a missing phase.

candidate.title: Candidate phases
candidate.scoreInfoIntroPre: The number on the right is
candidate.scoreInfoIntroPost: a pattern-fit quality — it's how well each phase passes the filters we have:
candidate.scoreInfoChemistry: does the phase contain only sample elements?
candidate.scoreInfoCrystalSystem: does it match the detected symmetry?
candidate.scoreInfoLattice: is the lattice parameter near the estimate (when available)?
candidate.scoreInfoBoost: for phases in your material preset's expected_phases list.
candidate.scoreInfoTieBold: multiple candidates have the same score
candidate.scoreInfoTiePost: , the constraints don't discriminate further. To know which phase this pixel actually is, run indexing — that correlates the pattern with each reference SHT and gives a real fit metric.
candidate.scoreInfoTieRanking: Ranking within ties: closer lattice → SHT-available → simpler structure (smaller n_atoms, so matrix-like phases rank ahead of complex polymorphs).
candidate.tiedWarningPost: at score {{score}}. The score is a constraint-pass-rate, not a pattern-fit quality. Run indexing for a real ranking.
candidate.filterChipsTooltip: Filter candidate phases: only expected, only SHT-available, or all.
candidate.emptyPre: No phase in the local library matches the symmetry + lattice + chemistry combination.
candidate.emptyBold: Pattern likely represents a phase not in your SHT library
candidate.offSystemBody: This phase's crystal system is not in the list of systems consistent with the detected symmetry. Score is multiplied by 0.5 as a penalty.
candidate.offSystemNote: ⚠ This can be a false-negative when the pattern shows multiple folds with similar NCCs (e.g. a tetragonal pattern viewed near [001] shows both 4-fold and 2-fold strongly; if 3-fold also happens to be high from noise, "cubic" wins and tetragonal phases get flagged). If indexing landed on this phase, trust the indexing — that uses the actual pattern correlation, not just symmetry heuristics.
candidate.degenerateBody: These phases share this one's space group and lattice (within 2%), so they produce the same Kikuchi pattern — EBSD geometry alone cannot tell them apart. Use chemistry (EDS) to decide between them.
candidate.fitIntro: The score is a product of multiple factors. These two are the pattern-derived ones:
candidate.fitSymBody: : how well the phase's primary rotation axes match the observed NCC peaks. Cubic on a 3-fold-strong pixel scores high; tetragonal (no 3-fold) scores lower.
candidate.fitDspBody: : how well the phase's theoretical d-spacings match the observed Hough bands. Larger d-spacings (lower-order reflections) are weighted higher because they're more informative + less noisy.
candidate.fitNote: Both are 0..1 (1 = perfect fit). Multiplied into the score so phases that actually fit the pattern rank above ones that only pass categorical filters.
candidate.externalEmpty: No external candidates found (or COD unreachable).
candidate.inLibraryBody: This phase's structure (space group + lattice) is already in your local library, so downloading its CIF adds nothing new. External search ranks novel phases first; this one is shown for comparison.
candidate.nextStep: Next step: generate the SHT in the Simulation tab (CIF → XTAL → MC → Master → SHT, ~30-60 min via WSL/EMsoft).
candidate.openInSimulationTooltip: Pre-fill the Simulation page with this CIF to generate its SHT master.
candidate.downloadCifTooltip: Download and save this external phase's CIF into your local library.
candidate.viewCifTooltip: Open the source CIF entry for this external candidate in a new tab.

pattern.title: Pattern preview
pattern.circularMaskTooltip: Clip the square detector corners to the inscribed disc on the pattern preview.
pattern.magnifierTooltip: Toggle a 3x zoom lens that follows the cursor over the pattern.
pattern.confidenceIntro: Colour of the zone-axis crosshair + n-fold arrows drawn on the pattern preview. Encodes how trustworthy the detected symmetry is:
pattern.confidenceHighBody: (NCC ≥ 0.55): clean zone-axis pattern, both fold and axis are reliable
pattern.confidenceMediumBody: (≥ 0.30): meaningful detection; the axis is broadly correct but the exact position may be off by a few pixels
pattern.confidenceLowBody: (≥ 0.15): weak hint; treat as "maybe", run indexing for a real answer
pattern.confidenceNote: Real raw EBSD patterns rarely reach high — most pixels land in medium or low. That's normal, not a bug.

symmetry.title: Symmetry
symmetry.methodSphericalBody: Method B projects each detector pixel to its 3D unit-vector direction, then rotates the sphere intensity field around candidate axes and computes the NCC. Works correctly for off-centre pattern centres + tilted detectors.
symmetry.methodSphericalAveraged: Averaged over {{count}} neighbouring patterns to suppress per-pixel noise (~2× NCC gain).
symmetry.methodSphericalThresholds: Confidence thresholds: HIGH ≥ 0.55, MEDIUM ≥ 0.30, LOW ≥ 0.15. Real raw patterns typically score 0.05–0.50.
symmetry.methodImageBody: Method A rotates the 2-D image around the brightest peak (or image centre) and computes the NCC. Fast, but fundamentally limited — real EBSD patterns have the PC off-centre and the detector tilted, so 3-D crystal symmetry doesn't appear as 2-D image symmetry.
symmetry.methodImageFallback: Used as fallback when detector geometry is unavailable.

lattice.title: Lattice parameter
lattice.infoIntro: A rough estimate of the lattice parameter a from Kikuchi band positions in the pattern (Hough transform → Bragg angles → d-spacings → lattice).
lattice.infoHighMediumBody: : ≥4 bands detected + d-spacing ratios match a known crystal family. The "Estimated a" is meaningful within ±20%.
lattice.infoNoneBody: : not enough bands found OR the d-spacing ratios don't match any cubic family. Common on noisy / off-axis / non-cubic patterns.
lattice.infoWhatToDoBody: When confidence is "none", trust the Symmetry section above instead. The lattice estimator is a coarse heuristic (band trace position ≠ band width); the symmetry detector is the more reliable signal.
lattice.infoRealMeasurement: For a real lattice measurement, run indexing — it correlates the pattern against reference SHTs (which include the exact lattice) and gives a calibrated answer.

clusters.title: Missing-phase candidates (not in local library)
clusters.empty: No clusters of unmatched pixels found. Either every analyzed pixel had a good library match, OR no clear symmetry was detected.
